9782 mádya¹ 'intoxicating' RV., n. 'spirituous liquor' Mn. [√mad¹]
    Pa. majja- n. 'intoxicant, wine, drinking-place'; Pk. majja- n. 'spirits'; M. māj̈ m. 'sexual heat'; Si. mada-ya 'arak'; — H. mājā m. 'foam on the water of the early rains'? — K. mas m. 'wine' see mádhu.
    *madya-² 'harrow' see matyà-.
    madrá- m. 'a country in North West India', pl. 'its people' ŚBr. [See malla-²]
    *madrarāṣṭra-.

13481 *supna 'dream'. [Cf. Gk. ὕπνος Mayrhofer HPa 45. — Direct derivation of Pa. supina- from IE. *supəno- is possible, but doubtful. — √svap¹]
    Pa. supina- m.n. 'dream', °aka- m., Pk. suviṇa-, sumiṇa-, siviṇa-, simiṇa-, siuṇa-, saviṇa- (-a- after vb. savaï) m., NiDoc. sumiṁna, Gy. eur. suno m., Bshk. sūn(a), Tor. sen f., Phal. sēn f.; WPah.roh. suina 'in a dream', jaun. swīṇō 'dream', Ku. swīṇo (whence swiṇṇo 'to dream, talk in one's sleep'), gng. swī˜ṛ̃, OB. suina, OG. sumiṇuṁ, samaṇaḍaüṁ n., G. samṇũ n., Si. sihina, sīnaya, hī° H. Smith JA 1950, 192. — S. suhaṇo m. 'dream', OG. suhaṇaüṁ n., G. sɔ(h)ṇũ n. poss. < śōbhana- 'something auspicious'.
    Addenda: *supna-: WPah.poet. sviṇo m. 'dream', kṭg. (kc.) sv̄́ṇɔ m. 'dream, (rarely) sleep'; — X MIA. suppati (see supyatē Add²): kṭg. súpṇɔ m. 'dream', J. supnā m., bhad. supṇũ n.
